Subject: Embeddings handoff: implementation timetable, vectorstore rationale, and rerank validation

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I’m sending a concise implementation plan for the embeddings + rerank handoff so your engineering and search teams can review before we lock the cutover window. High-level items below; attachments contain the sample queries and the vectorstore evaluation matrix.

Key goals:
- Produce seeded embeddings for 8M content items (phase 1) with acceptance QA for rerank.
- Choose vectorstore that supports nearest-neighbor >1M vectors, multi-tenant namespace isolation, and incremental backfill without downtime.
- Establish rerank evaluation set (3k queries) and pass-fail criteria before production traffic split.

Proposed timetable (draft):
1) Oct 7–9: kickoff + access provisioning (you provide service account, we validate S3 permissions).
2) Oct 10–14: sample embedding run (10k records) + sanity rerank baseline.
3) Oct 15–21: vectorstore benchmark (throughput/latency/recall) — see attached matrix.
4) Oct 22–28: parallel backfill (staggered by shard) + smoke tests.
5) Oct 29–31: rerank A/B 10% traffic; acceptance gating.

Decision points we need from Acme:
- Vectorstore preference (we recommend Faiss on managed clusters OR Pinecone for fully managed).
- Backfill window constraints for index writes (can you accept rolling index writes during business hours?).
- Primary rerank metric for acceptance (MRR@10 or nDCG@10).

Action items: please review the attached sample queries and the vectorstore pros/cons doc. If the timetable works, confirm service account + S3 details and we’ll schedule the Oct 7 kickoff.

Thanks,
Mina

Folks —

I ran a quick local micro-benchmark against a 2M-vector sample using Faiss (IVF+PQ) and a small Pinecone trial instance. Summary for the matrix:

Pros / Cons (short):
- Faiss (self-managed): +lowest per-query latency in local runs; +flexible quantization tuning; -requires ops for shard management and snapshotting; -restore time on node failure can be slow without additional tooling.
- Pinecone (managed): +fully managed scaling and snapshotting; +APIs for namespaces and vectors per tenant; -higher steady-state cost; -some limits on custom compression knobs.

Operational note: since Acme requires rolling writes during 1am–5am, Faiss backfill will need careful shard throttling and a leader election mechanism (we propose small coordinator lambda to enforce per-shard QPS). Pinecone supports background upserts with built-in throttling which reduces ops complexity.

Rerank eval: for nDCG@10 acceptance we should run a 3k query set with human-labelled top-10 relevance for a subset (300 queries). Proposed pass criteria: nDCG@10 > baseline + 8% and no regression in top-1 for more than 5% of queries. I’ll attach the micro-benchmark logs to the Drive link.

I’ll prepare an ops snippet for Faiss backfill throttler and a Pinecone cost-estimate mock.

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Sarah —

Appreciate the quick answers. Based on Aditya’s notes and your preference for managed, here are two recommended paths and the decision implications:

Option A — Pinecone (managed):
- Pros: minimal ops, simplified backfill, snapshots, multi-namespace isolation.
- Cons: higher annual cost; need procurement review (Karthik will run SOC2 check).
- Acceptance gating: run 10k sample + 3k rerank eval, if pass -> proceed to parallel backfill.

Option B — Faiss (self-managed on customer cluster):
- Pros: lower long-term cost, finer control over PQ/IVF; better tail latencies in tests.
- Cons: requires infra support from Acme; we’ll provide backfill throttler; longer RTO on node failure.

Next actions I’ll execute after you confirm preferred path:
- If Pinecone: Marissa will request procurement approvals; we’ll schedule a pricing review and SOC2 evidence exchange.
- If Faiss: Aditya will spin up the backfill throttler runbook and we’ll do a dry-run with 10k records.

Can you confirm preference by Oct 6 so we can lock the Oct 7 kickoff?

Thanks,
Mina
